paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson: no army, no boast and no pile of chariots is bigger than the Lord GOD of Hosts. Egypt rose like the Nile and boasted, 'I will rise and cover the earth' (Jeremiah 46:8). Then the passage says, 'For that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts' (Jeremiah 46:10). Egypt had the plan, the shields and the horses, and the day still wasn't theirs.

Now look at what that does to us. We all have a version of that boast, like 'I've got this handled,' and I have said it right before burning a whole batch. Egypt is told to go up to Gilead for balm, yet the Lord says, 'In vain you try many remedies, but for you there is no healing' (Jeremiah 46:11). So the safest place to stand is under His word, not on our own strength.

Here's why that's good news for you, baker. The nations heard of Egypt's shame (Jeremiah 46:12), and the whole world could see who held the day. That means the One you follow is not nervous about any power on earth. Keep your eyes on Him, keep your ovens ready, and let the boasting be somebody else's job.
